AI Chief of Staff

Less routine work. More thoughtful control.

PROJECT CONTEXTPersonal learning project
PROFILE DATEJune 2026
TOOLS & APPROACHStreamlit · Gemini · Gmail & Calendar APIs · MCP

The question

Email and meeting coordination contain many small decisions: what needs attention, what context matters, and what should happen next. An assistant can help prepare that work, while the person remains responsible for what is sent.

An assistant with a review step

UnderstandTriage messages and gather context
PrepareDraft a response or check availability
ReviewApprove, edit, regenerate, or reject

Human review sketch

AI preparesYou reviewYou decide

My project entry describes an approval-gated email workflow, Gmail and Google Calendar integrations through MCP, personalized draft generation, and scheduling with availability checks.

The business analysis lens

Automation is most useful when its boundaries are clear. In this workflow, the approval step is part of the process design, not an afterthought.

  • Decision rights: distinguish what the assistant can prepare from what a person approves.
  • Exceptions: account for missing information, rejected drafts, and unavailable meeting times.
  • Traceability: keep the selected action and the reviewed content connected.
  • Adoption: make review simple enough that people can remain meaningfully involved.

Why this work interests me

Operations and training both depend on clear handoffs. This project connects that interest with AI: making the routine parts easier while keeping important decisions understandable.

What this currently demonstrates

A personal prototype exploring AI assistance with human approval, clear handoffs, and useful alternatives when a draft needs more work. The workflow sketch shows the idea behind the project.
